specification.title: A transactional migration's reversal deletes its marker and then fails
steps: Revert. m1's reversal deletes its marker and then raises an error. The migration is transactional, so the deletion is in the reversal's transaction.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the revert has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If a migration's reversal fails, the operation reports failure and the migration's history entry remains; for a transactional migration, its marker also remains.

execution.description: Positive control. PDO::beginTransaction, prepared inserts, then PDO::commit or PDO::rollBack. A caught statement error calls rollBack() and does not call commit(). A thrown rollBack() or commit() drops the handle and is reported as failed, not as a confirmed rollback. ATTR_PERSISTENT is false. One connection, not a pool. The command tag is not read.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: A reported failure says the revert did not complete. For a transactional migration, the caller can treat the migration as still applied.

evaluation.reason: PDO has no migration runner or reversible migration history. This adapter does not add one.

reproduction.requires: pnpm run setup, then pnpm run pg:up (README.md)
